Trouvailles :

Il y a des changements dégénératifs sévères au niveau patellofémoral avec une perte de cartilage complète à la facette latérale de la rotule et au niveau de l’apex puis impliquant aussi la partie latérale de la trochlée du fémur avec des changements réactifs sous-chondraux. Conclusion :

Changements dégénératifs sévères au niveau patellofémoral et légers à modérés des compartiments interne et externe.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: [IDENTIFIER]. Derangement of collateral ligament of knee, left 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Minimal marrow edema in the lateral aspect of the fibular head. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is focal cartilage thinning with underlying subchondral cyst of the posterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: There is tendinosis of the distal quadriceps tendon, greatest medially. There is edema and borderline thickening in the adjacent anterior suprapatellar fat pad which could represent anterior suprapatellar fat pad impingement syndrome if there is clinical correlation.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Findings which could represent mild left anterior suprapatellar fat pad syndrome for which clinical correlation is recommended.
2.	Adjacent distal quadriceps tendinosis.
3.	Focal cartilage thinning with associated subchondral cyst of the posterior medial femoral condyle.


Addendum:

There is mild increased T2 signal in the common peroneal nerve along the lateral aspect of the left fibular head and neck compatible with common peroneal neuropathy. There is mild edema in the visualized anterior compartment muscles which could represent denervation edema. Very small Baker's cyst.

Findings:  There is a minor knee effusion. There is a horizontal tear through the posterior horn and posterior body of the medial meniscus. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral articular cartilage is preserved. Mild - moderate thinning of the lateral patellofemoral articular cartilage is noted with mild underlying bony change.  
Conclusion: Tearing of the medial meniscus. Lateral patellofemoral degeneration.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Tendinitis patelar izquierda.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios categóricos de rotura.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales dentro de límites conservados.
Cartílago troclear dentro de límites normales.
Condropatía superficial de la faceta lateral y vértice de la rótula, sin cambios óseos secundarios.
No hay derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura. Tendón
cuadricipital, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites
normales.
Leve aumento de señal de las partes blandas entre la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.
Discreto edema del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
Discreto edema de la región prepatelar sin colecciones líquidas categóricas.
Impresión:
Condropatía superficial de la faceta lateral y vértice de la rótula.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal.
Probables fenómenos de fricción de la banda iliotibial y de hiperpresión externa de la rótula.
Discreto edema de la región prepatelar sin colecciones líquidas regionales

> Curvilinear subchondral abnormal signal area breached the articular surface in medial femoral condyle with heterogenous signal on F/S T2WI, C/W osteonecrosis (SONK, spontaneous osteonecrosis of knee); bone marrow edema in medial femoral condyle.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear.
> No strong MR evidence of tear of lateral meniscus.
> Wearing of articular cartilage of left knee, more severe at medial femoral condyle ( grade 3-4 chondromalacia), reflecting osteoarthritis.
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal with intermediate signal ntensity inside on T1WI.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.

Impression: 
1. C/W osteonecrosis in centroinfeior portion of left medial femoral condyle (stage III) and bone marrow edema.
2. Osteoarthritis of left knee, more severe at medial compartment.
3. Tear of posteiror horn of medial meniscus.
4. Synovitis of left knee and suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: pain; bilateral knee pain for 8 months, no injury
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Mild tricompartmental osteophytic spurring.


JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. Ossified body in the anterior intercondylar notch measuring 0.8 cm. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Myxoid degeneration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus without tear.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the weightbearing medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Myxoid degeneration of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus with undersurface tear of the body/posterior horn junction.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Small area of full-thickness cartilage loss along the weightbearing lateral tibial plateau with subchondral edema with low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the weightbearing lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Multifocal areas of full-thickness cartilage loss along the medial facet, median ridge, lateral facet, and lateral femoral trochlea with underlying subchondral edema

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Lateral patellar tilt and translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Top normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 16 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION: 
1.	Undersurface tear at the junction of the body/posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.
2.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, most advanced in the patellofemoral compartment.
3.	Findings of lateral patellofemoral maltracking with edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad, lateral patellar tilt and translation, top normal TT-TG, and patellofemoral chondrosis. 
4.	Small joint effusion with ossified body in the anterior intercondylar notch.
